from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Vector: Magnitude and Direction", [
            "Scalars are simple numbers like five meters.",
            "Vectors represent both magnitude and direction.",
            "Imagine a squirrel running North-East."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a vector
        vector = Arrow(start=self.grid['E1'], end=self.grid['B4'], buff=0)
        vector.set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(vector))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display length
        label = MathTex("5", color="#FFD700")
        label.next_to(vector, UP, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight head
        dot = Dot(point=vector.get_end(), color="#FF4500")
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):

            "Define components as horizontal and vertical steps.",
            "Think of robot movement like (3, 4)."

        # Components

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Create(vec))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule", 
                          ["Connect vectors using the tip-to-tail rule.", 
                           "The resultant is the path from start to finish.", 
                           "A boat path diverted by current."])
        
        # Define vectors
        vec1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color="#FFFFFF", buff=0)
        vec2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=DOWN*2, color="#FFD700", buff=0)
        resultant = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2 + DOWN*2, color="#FF4500", buff=0)
        
        # Helper to position
        self.place_at_grid(vec1, 'B2')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), Create(vec1))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Position vec2 tail at vec1 tip
        vec2.move_to(vec1.get_end() + DOWN*1, aligned_edge=UP)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), Create(vec2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF4500"), Create(resultant))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Scalars scale a vector's total length.", 
            "Direction remains constant for positive scalars.", 
            "A superhero jump: double length, same direction."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Scalar Multiplication: Scaling Reality", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Application", 
                          ["Vectors simplify movement in physics simulations.", 
                           "Component addition determines object paths.", 
                           "Game characters use these for jumping."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in a collection of previous vector examples
        v1 = Vector([1, 1], color=WHITE)
        v2 = Vector([-0.5, 1.5], color=WHITE)
        vecs = VGroup(v1, v2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(vecs, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(vecs))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate the vectors interacting in a simple physics simulation
        v_sum = Vector([0.5, 2.5], color="#00BFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(v_sum, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(vecs.animate.set_opacity(0.3), GrowArrow(v_sum))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00BFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display text 'Vectors govern physical motion' on screen
        motion_text = Text("Vectors govern physical motion", font_size=32, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_in_area(motion_text, "E1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(motion_text))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: Vectors in Motion
outline.target_audience: High school students or introductory university students

sections.title: Defining the Vector: Magnitude and Direction
sections.content: Introduce a vector as a directed arrow representing both magnitude (length) and direction. Contrast this with scalars (simple numbers).
sections.example: A squirrel running 5 meters North-East; the arrow represents the displacement.

sections.title: Visualization via Coordinate Systems
sections.content: Explain how to place vectors on a 2D Cartesian plane (x, y). Define components as the horizontal and vertical 'steps' taken to reach the tip of the arrow from the tail.
sections.example: Representing a robot's movement as (3, 4), meaning 3 units right and 4 units up on a grid.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
sections.content: Demonstrate the geometric method of adding vectors by placing the tail of the second vector at the tip of the first. Explain that the result (resultant) is the direct path from start to finish.
sections.example: A boat traveling East, then diverted by a river current South; the resultant arrow shows the actual path relative to the shore.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Scaling Reality
sections.content: Show how multiplying a vector by a scalar constant changes its length without changing its original orientation (unless the scalar is negative).
sections.example: A superhero jumping: if vector 'v' is a jump, '2v' is a jump twice as long in the exact same direction.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Briefly synthesize how vectors simplify complex movements in gaming engines and physics simulations by breaking them down into manageable coordinate components.
sections.example: A video game character jumping: velocity vectors are calculated using these exact component additions to determine landing coordinates.
